category: off-by-one boundary condition in a greedy line filler; two packages, layered helpers
issue: Wrapping text to a fixed width loses one usable column. A word that would end exactly on the width boundary is pushed onto the next line instead of staying put. Wrapping "one two three" to 7 columns produces three lines ("one", "two", "three") even though "one two" is exactly 7 characters wide and should share a line. Every paragraph comes out more ragged than it needs to be, and the effect gets worse at narrow widths.

reference_fix.old: if current and used + gap + len(word) >= width:
reference_fix.new: if current and used + gap + len(word) > width:
